children: Adani New Industries Limited (ANIL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Adani Enterprises
, has commenced manufacturing 91.2-metre wind turbine blades at its facility in Mundra, Gujarat, marking a milestone for India's wind energy equipment industry, the company said in a statement.
The blades, the longest ever manufactured in India, are designed for the company's 5 MW MWL185-5.0 platform, which has also received certification, clearing the way for commercial series production.

The new turbine platform features a 185-metre rotor diameter and a hub height of 140 metres. Its swept area of approximately 26,600 square metres is equivalent to more than three and a half football pitches. The larger rotor is designed to capture more wind energy, enabling higher electricity generation even at sites with relatively low wind speeds. This could make additional locations across India viable for wind power development.

The new blade follows the 78.6-metre and 80.5-metre variants already being manufactured at the Mundra facility. The expansion of its blade portfolio reflects Adani Wind's efforts to develop larger and more efficient turbine platforms for the domestic renewable energy market.

The MWL185-5.0 platform was certified by Germany-based independent testing organisation WindGuard Certification GmbH following trials of a prototype installed at Mundra. The assessment confirmed compliance with the International Electrotechnical Commission's IEC 61400 standards for wind turbines. Adani developed the platform in collaboration with its German technology partner, W2E (Wind to Energy).

Milind Kulkarni, chief executive officer of Adani Wind, said the development would help expand the geographical potential of wind energy in India by making power generation more viable at locations with lower wind speeds. He said the company would continue developing and manufacturing advanced wind energy technologies domestically to support the country's growing clean energy requirements.

Adani Wind is the only Indian manufacturer featured in BloombergNEF's 2025 ranking of the world's 15 leading wind turbine manufacturers. Three of its turbine platforms are included in the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy's approved list of wind turbine models and manufacturers.

The company's MWL160-5.2 MW turbine has crossed 2 GW in cumulative installations at Khavda in Gujarat, which hosts the world's largest renewable energy park. Adani Wind has also secured more than 1 GW of orders from independent power producers outside the Adani Group, indicating growing demand from third-party customers.

Adani Wind currently has an annual manufacturing capacity of 2.25 GW and plans to increase production capacity as demand expands. Alongside its manufacturing operations in India, the company operates a technology centre in Rostock, Germany, supporting its turbine development and engineering capabilities.

title: Adani unveils India's longest wind turbine blades in Gujarat
